name: Satellite and Cable II Directive
evidence_rating: none: qualitative forecasts only; no baseline data, no review report found and no independent studies found
summary: The Directive aimed to make more TV and radio programmes available online across borders by simplifying copyright clearance for broadcasters' online services and for internet-based retransmission. The Commission promised to monitor cross-border availability but no data have been published, the review due in June 2025 has not been found, and no independent study has measured the effects.

indicators.objective: The proposal's financial statement has no indicators section; the memorandum promised baseline data collection at entry into force and monitoring of cross-border availability of TV and radio programmes every two to three years. Article 13 required a review report by 7 June 2025, which was not found published

indicators.indicator: Cross-border availability of TV and radio programmes (incl. broadcasters' ancillary online services)
indicators.evidence: No baseline or monitoring data found.

indicators.indicator: Lower rights-clearance costs for broadcasters' cross-border online services and for retransmission over closed networks (e.g. IPTV)
indicators.evidence: Not quantified ex ante or measured ex post.

indicators.indicator: Benefits for consumers, impact on creative industries and on investment in new content

literature.citation: European Commission (2016), Impact Assessment on the modernisation of EU copyright rules (executive summary SWD(2016) 302), SWD(2016) 301
literature.title: Impact Assessment on the modernisation of EU copyright rules (executive summary SWD(2016) 302)
literature.outcomes: rights-clearance costs; cross-border availability of broadcasts
literature.headline: Country-of-origin principle for broadcasters' ancillary online services and mandatory collective management for retransmission over closed networks would reduce transaction costs and enhance cross-border distribution of and access to TV and radio programmes; benefits not quantified
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected simpler copyright clearance to make more TV and radio programmes available online across borders, but did not put a number on the gain.
literature.quality: forecast; qualitative only; the adopted scope was narrowed to news, current affairs and fully financed own productions
